claims.text: Steel components in hot-dip aluminum equipment are vulnerable to attack by high-temperature molten aluminum.
Applying a high-alumina ceramic coating to steel contact surfaces can significantly reduce corrosive erosion by molten aluminum.
Thermal spraying is an appropriate method for depositing the proposed high-alumina coating.
Chemical vapor deposition is an appropriate method for depositing the proposed high-alumina coating.
The coating will form a dense Al2O3 barrier.
The Al2O3 barrier will adhere to the steel substrate during service.
A dense, adherent Al2O3 barrier resists chemical reaction with molten aluminum.
Alumina has a high melting point.
Alumina is chemically inert toward liquid aluminum under the proposed operating conditions.
Alumina's high melting point and chemical inertness reduce chemical interactions with liquid aluminum.
Reduced chemical interaction prevents or slows penetration of aluminum into the steel substrate.
Slower aluminum penetration reduces overall erosion of the component.
High-alumina-coated parts will have a lower material-loss or corrosion rate than uncoated or conventionally coated parts under identical exposure conditions.
High-alumina-coated parts will retain dimensional integrity longer than uncoated or conventionally coated parts.
Equipment without specialized high-alumina coatings undergoes rapid erosion during regular contact with high-temperature aluminum.
Erosion caused by regular molten-aluminum contact decreases equipment service life.
Thermal cycling, mechanical wear, and thermal-expansion mismatch may reduce coating effectiveness by weakening adhesion or causing spallation.
Impurities in the aluminum bath may affect the coating's long-term behavior.
Mass loss, surface morphology, coating integrity, post-exposure adhesion, and corrosion rate can be measured to compare coated and control samples.
The hypothesis is falsified if coated samples show no statistically significant improvement over controls or suffer severe spallation within the expected service life.
